newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU money to translate books from minority tongues.
newsitem.headline: EU money to translate books from minority tongues.

text.p: Welsh and Luxemburgisch poetry books, Flemish or Basque novels, Lapp dramas and Breton encyclopaedias may be translated into English or French under a new European Union plan to be launched this week.
The European Union will release seven million Ecus ($7.7 million) to help translate books written in the bloc's lesser-known tongues into a language in which they can be more widely read.
Euro-MPs complain that difficulties writers in lesser-known languages face in being translated left the book market dominated by English best-sellers
The two-year plan, named Ariane, will be nodded through by EU budget ministers on Thursday after approval by the European Parliament last week.

"This is something that will bring cultures and citizens closer together and help create a Europe of the citizens," Nana Mouskouri, the multilingual Greek singer and Member of Parliament responsible for the programme, told the assembly.
The EU has 11 official languages and around 40 languages overall, and the linguistic web is set to grow early next century when the EU plans to take in five new countries from eastern Europe.
